baseline:
C
Turbulent flow is defined by its chaotic, irregular motion and the presence of swirling eddies, in contrast to the smooth, layered, and predictable motion of laminar flow.

B
Vectors have both magnitude and direction, whereas scalars only have magnitude. In a velocity field, the velocity at any point is a vector because it specifies both the speed and the direction of the fluid's motion. A scalar quantity in the same field, like pressure or temperature, would only have a value (magnitude) at that point.

A
The Kolmogorov constant (C_K) is the empirical, dimensionless constant of proportionality in the Kolmogorov five-thirds law for the energy spectrum of turbulent flows.

B
The energy cascade is the process in which energy is injected into a turbulent flow at large scales (large eddies), then transferred to progressively smaller eddies, and finally dissipated into heat by viscosity at the smallest scales.

C
The energy spectrum E(k) is directly proportional to ε^(2/3). An increase in the energy dissipation rate (ε) will therefore increase the energy level across all wavenumbers, causing the entire curve to shift upward.
